stories.why_ar: قصّة مبنيّة على الشرط الثاني و«wish»: ماذا لو حصلتَ على كلّ ما تتمنّاه؟
lines: King Midas was already the richest man in his country, but he always wanted more.
"If everything I touched turned to gold," he often said, "I would be the happiest man alive."
One day a god heard him and decided to give him exactly what he had asked for.
The next morning, the king touched his bed, and it became gold.
He touched a chair, a door and a tree in the garden, and they were all turned into gold.
Midas laughed and ran from room to room, touching everything he could find.
At lunch he was so hungry that he picked up a piece of bread.
Before he could eat it, the bread had become a hard yellow stone.
He tried to drink some water, but it was gold before it reached his lips.
Just then his little daughter ran into the room and threw her arms around him.
In a second, she was standing still, a statue made of gold.
The king fell to his knees and cried, "I wish I had never asked for this gift!"
The god told him to wash his hands in the river if he wanted to lose his power.
Midas ran to the river, and as the water touched him, the gold disappeared.
His daughter was brought back to life, and she was laughing again.
From that day on, Midas said that a warm hand was worth more than all the gold in the world.
stories.moral_en: Some wishes are dangerous because they come true.
stories.moral_ar: بعض الأمنيات خطيرة لأنّها تتحقّق فعلاً.

stories.why_ar: مليئة بالكلام المنقول: قال لهم، طلب منهم، سألهم — وهي من دروس الأسبوع 22.
lines: A tired traveller arrived in a small village late one cold evening.
He had walked all day and had not eaten anything since the morning.
He knocked on several doors, but everyone told him that they had no food to share.
So he made a fire in the middle of the village and put a large pot of water on it.
Then he took a smooth stone out of his bag and dropped it into the water.
A curious woman asked him what he was cooking.
"Stone soup," he answered. "It is delicious, but it would be even better with an onion."
The woman said that she had one onion at home, and she went to get it.
A man who had been watching brought two carrots, because he wanted to taste the soup too.
Soon a child appeared with some potatoes, and an old farmer brought salt and a little meat.
Each person who passed added something small to the pot.
After an hour, the whole village was sitting around the fire, eating hot soup together.
Everyone agreed that they had never tasted such a wonderful soup.
The next morning, the traveller thanked them and said goodbye.
He left the stone behind and told them they could use it again.
Of course, it was not the stone that had made the soup, and by then everyone knew it.
stories.moral_en: When everyone gives a little, there is enough for all.
stories.moral_ar: حين يعطي كلّ واحدٍ قليلاً، يكفي الجميع.

stories.why_ar: قصّة عن الخوف من قول الحقيقة، وفيها المبني للمجهول في كلّ مكان: was made, was seen, was told.
lines: There was once an emperor who loved new clothes more than anything else.
One day, two men came to the palace and said that they were the best weavers in the world.
They promised to make him clothes from a very special cloth.
"Anyone who is stupid or bad at his job will not be able to see it," they explained.
The emperor paid them a lot of gold, and the men started working on an empty machine.
Of course, there was no cloth at all, because the two men were thieves.
The emperor sent his oldest minister to see how the work was going.
The minister could not see anything, but he was afraid that people would think he was stupid.
So he told the emperor that the cloth was beautiful.
Finally, the emperor was dressed in his new clothes, which nobody could see.
He walked through the city, and all the people shouted, "What wonderful clothes!"
Nobody wanted to be the first to say what they really saw.
Then a small boy pointed and said, "But he isn't wearing anything!"
The words were repeated from person to person until the whole crowd was laughing.
The emperor knew that the boy was right, but he kept walking with his head held high.
By then, the two thieves had already left the city with the gold.
stories.moral_en: The truth does not need everyone's permission to be true.
stories.moral_ar: الحقيقة لا تحتاج إلى موافقة الجميع لتكون حقيقة.

stories.why_ar: جحا من جديد، في مستوى أعلى: الماضي التامّ والكلام المنقول وجمل الوصل.
lines: One day, Juha was invited to a wedding party at the house of a rich merchant.
He had been working in his garden all morning, so he went in his old, dirty clothes.
When he arrived, nobody looked at him, and nobody offered him a seat.
The servants who were carrying the food walked past him as if he were not there.
After an hour, Juha quietly left the party and went home.
He washed, and he put on the most beautiful coat that he owned.
When he returned, the merchant himself came to the door to welcome him.
He was given the best seat in the room, and the finest dishes were placed in front of him.
Juha took a piece of meat and pushed it into the sleeve of his coat.
Then he poured some soup over the coat and said, "Eat, my coat! Eat!"
The guests stopped talking and stared at him.
The merchant asked him why he was feeding his clothes.
Juha explained that an hour earlier he had come in his old clothes and nobody had noticed him.
"Now I have come back in this coat, and I am treated like a king," he said.
"So it is clear that the food was not for me. It was for my coat."
The merchant's face turned red, and the guests looked down at their plates.
stories.moral_en: Judge people by who they are, not by what they wear.
stories.moral_ar: احكم على الناس بما هم عليه، لا بما يلبسون.

stories.why_ar: كلّ طلب فيها يبدأ بـ«wish» أو «if»: الشرط الثاني في قصّة كاملة.
lines: A poor fisherman lived with his wife in a small hut near the sea.
One day he caught a large fish that could speak.
"Please let me go," said the fish. "I am not really a fish. I am a prince under a spell."
The kind fisherman put it back into the water and went home with nothing.
When he told his wife what had happened, she was angry.
"You should have asked for something!" she shouted. "I wish we lived in a nice cottage."
The fisherman went back to the sea and called the fish, who agreed at once.
When he got home, the hut had been replaced by a pretty cottage with a garden.
But a week later his wife said, "If we lived in a castle, I would be truly happy."
The fish gave them a castle, and soon after that she wanted to be queen.
Each time the fisherman went to the sea, the water was darker and the wind was stronger.
Finally, his wife said that she wished she could control the sun and the moon.
The fisherman was afraid, but he went to the sea one last time.
The waves were as high as mountains, and he had to shout to be heard.
"Go home," said the fish quietly. "She is back in her old hut."
And there they still live, if they have not died, in the same small hut by the sea.
stories.moral_en: The person who always wants more is never satisfied.
stories.moral_ar: مَن يريد المزيد دائماً لا يشبع أبداً.

stories.why_ar: نهاية مفاجئة تقوم على الماضي التامّ: ما كان قد حدث قبل أن تعرف.
lines: Mathilde was a young woman who dreamed of a life of money and beautiful things.
Her husband was a simple office worker, and they lived in a small apartment.
One evening he came home happily with an invitation to an important party.
Mathilde started to cry, because she had no jewellery to wear with her dress.
So she visited a rich friend, who lent her a wonderful diamond necklace.
At the party she was the most admired woman in the room, and she danced all night.
But when she got home, she realised that the necklace had disappeared.
They searched the streets and the taxi, but it was never found.
They borrowed money from everyone they knew and bought a new necklace that looked the same.
Mathilde returned it to her friend, who did not notice the difference.
For ten years the couple worked day and night to pay back what they had borrowed.
Mathilde washed floors and carried water, and her hands became rough and red.
One day she met her friend in the park and told her the whole story.
Her friend took her hands and looked at her with great sadness.
"Oh, my poor Mathilde," she said. "Mine was not real. It was worth almost nothing."
If Mathilde had told the truth ten years earlier, everything would have been different.
stories.moral_en: Pride can cost more than the truth.
stories.moral_ar: الكِبر قد يكلّف أكثر من قول الحقيقة.

stories.why_ar: عن وعدٍ نُقض: المبني للمجهول والكلام المنقول في قصّة واحدة.
lines: Many years ago, the town of Hamelin was full of rats.
They were found in every kitchen, every bed and every shoe.
The people were desperate, and they begged the mayor to do something.
One morning, a strange man in a red and yellow coat arrived with a small pipe.
He told the mayor that he could remove every rat if the town paid him a thousand gold coins.
The mayor agreed immediately, because he was sure that it was impossible.
The man began to play a sweet, strange tune as he walked through the streets.
Rats came out of every house and followed him down to the river, where they were all drowned.
But when the piper asked for his money, the mayor only laughed.
He said that the rats were already dead, so the job had been too easy to be worth a thousand coins.
The piper did not argue. He just smiled and lifted his pipe again.
This time, a different tune was heard, and it was the children who came out of the houses.
They followed him, dancing and singing, out of the town and towards the mountains.
Their parents tried to stop them, but it was as if they could not move.
The children were never seen in Hamelin again.
People say that the mayor wished, for the rest of his life, that he had kept his promise.
stories.moral_en: A promise has to be kept, even when it seems too easy.
stories.moral_ar: الوعد يُوفى به، حتى حين يبدو العمل سهلاً.

stories.why_ar: قصّة حبّ قصيرة بنهاية مزدوجة، تُبنى كلّها على ما كان قد فعله كلٌّ منهما سرّاً.
lines: It was the day before the holiday, and Della had only one dollar and eighty-seven cents.
She had saved every coin for months, but it was not enough to buy a present for her husband, Jim.
The couple had only two treasures.
One was Jim's gold watch, which had belonged to his father and grandfather.
The other was Della's hair, which was long, brown and beautiful.
Della looked in the mirror for a long time, and then she put on her old coat and went out.
An hour later she came home with short hair and twenty dollars.
With the money she had bought a fine gold chain for Jim's watch.
When Jim came home and saw her, he stood at the door without moving.
"Don't look at me like that," Della said. "My hair will grow again, I promise."
Jim took a small box out of his pocket and gave it to her.
Inside were two beautiful combs for her long hair — the combs she had wanted for years.
Della held them and smiled through her tears.
Then she gave him the chain and asked him to put it on his watch.
Jim sat down, smiled and said quietly, "I sold the watch to buy your combs."
Each of them had given away the thing they loved most, and each gift was now useless — and perfect.
stories.moral_en: The best gift is what you are willing to give up.
stories.moral_ar: أجمل هديّة هي ما تتخلّى عنه من أجل مَن تحبّ.

stories.source_ar: واشنطن إرفنغ — ريب فان وينكل، أُعيدت كتابتها
stories.why_ar: رجل يستيقظ فيجد كلّ شيء قد تغيّر: أفضل تمرين على الماضي التامّ.
lines: Rip was a friendly man who lived in a village at the foot of the mountains.
Everyone liked him, but he hated hard work, and his wife was always angry with him.
One autumn day, he took his dog and his gun and walked up into the mountains to escape.
Near the top, he met a group of strange old men who were playing a game.
They gave him something to drink, and soon he felt very tired and lay down under a tree.
When he woke up, his dog had gone, and his gun was old and covered in rust.
His beard had grown long and white, and his legs were stiff.
He walked slowly back to the village, but he did not recognise anyone.
His house was empty, and the roof had fallen in.
The people stared at him and asked who he was.
He said his name was Rip and asked about his old friends.
They told him that one had died and another had moved to the city years before.
Then a young woman stepped forward, holding a baby.
"My father was called Rip," she said. "He went into the mountains twenty years ago and never came back."
Rip looked at her and realised that he had slept for twenty years.
He spent the rest of his life sitting outside the village shop, telling his story to anyone who would listen.
stories.moral_en: Time does not wait for anyone.

stories.why_ar: أطول قصّة في المكتبة وأغناها: المبني للمجهول وجمل الوصل والكلام المنقول معاً.
lines: High above the city stood the statue of the Happy Prince.
He was covered with thin leaves of gold, his eyes were two blue jewels, and a red ruby shone on his sword.
One cold night, a little bird who was flying south for the winter stopped to rest at his feet.
Suddenly, a drop of water fell on her. The prince was crying.
"When I was alive, I never saw sadness," he said. "Now I can see all the misery of my city."
He asked the bird to take the ruby from his sword to a poor woman whose son was ill.
The bird did not want to stay, but she agreed, just for one night.
The next day, the prince asked her to take one of his eyes to a young writer who had no money for food.
Then the other eye was given to a little girl who sold matches in the street.
"Now you are blind," said the bird, "so I will stay with you always."
Every day she took a leaf of gold from his body and gave it to someone in need.
Soon the prince was grey and ugly, and the bird was too weak to fly in the snow.
One morning she kissed him, fell down at his feet and died, and his heart broke.
The mayor said that the statue was so ugly that it should be removed and melted.
But the broken heart would not melt, so it was thrown away with the dead bird.
It is said that these were the two most precious things that were ever found in that city.
stories.moral_en: Real beauty is in what we give, not in what we wear.
stories.moral_ar: الجمال الحقيقيّ فيما نعطي، لا فيما نلبس.
